DATA:
Event: first discovery.
When: year 37, early winter, morning.
Place: Harum (their word; it means "cold hollow"), the winter camp of the Kesh band.
People:
- Imra: woman, 19 years old, of the Kesh band.
- Tavu: man, 23 years old, of the Kesh band; brother of Imra.
What happened, in order:
- Imra was shaping a scraper by striking cutting stone against a lump of heavy yellow stone.
- Sparks fell on dry moss beside her, and the moss began to smoke.
- Imra blew on the smoking moss, and it caught fire.
- She tried again 3 times that day, and the moss caught fire 2 of those times.
- Tavu saw it.
- Before this, the Kesh band kept fire only by carrying embers from camp to camp.
- This was the first time anyone in the world made fire by striking stones.
Beliefs (not facts):
- Imra believed (but was not sure): fire lives inside the heavy yellow stone.
Their own words for things (use these): "cutting stone", "heavy yellow stone".

DATA:
Event: death from cold.
When: year 41, deep winter, night.
Place: Harum (their word; it means "cold hollow"), the old winter camp of the Kesh band.
Other place: Ulmeke (their word; it means "red cliff"), a camp 4 days' walk away.
People:
- Oru: man, 58 years old, of the Kesh band.
- Sefi: woman, 34 years old, of the Kesh band; daughter of Oru.

- In autumn, Oru broke his leg in a fall, and after that he could not walk far.
- Food ran out at Harum, so the Kesh band moved to Ulmeke, a walk of 4 days.

- Sefi was the last to leave him.
- On his 4th night alone, the fire went out and Oru died of cold.
- 10 days later, 2 hunters of the band found his body beside the dead fire.

DATA:
Event: feud killing.
When: year 63, late summer, dusk.
Place: Teshu (their word; it means "shallow crossing"), a ford of the river.
People:
- Anuk: man, 31 years old, of the Kesh band.
- Moro: man, 27 years old, of the Tulo band.

- Pell: man, of the Kesh band; brother of Anuk, dead since spring.

- Anuk waited for Moro at Teshu.
- When Moro came to cross, Anuk killed him with a spear thrust to the belly. The spear had a cutting stone point.
- Moro died at the ford before dark.

- Ishe ran to the Tulo camp and told them.

- Anuk believed (and was sure): Moro killed his brother Pell in the spring. (This belief is why Anuk killed Moro.)
Known to the world but not to the people:
- In truth, Pell drowned in the river in the spring. No one killed him.
Their own words for things (use these): "cutting stone".

DATA:
Event: band split.
When: year 70, autumn.
Place: Ulmeke (their word; it means "red cliff"), a cliff with dry caves.
Other place: Kotara (their word; it means "salt shore"), the sea shore, 6 days' walk away.

- The Amaru band, 26 people, argued for 2 days at Ulmeke about where to spend the winter.
- Hesh wanted to go to Kotara.
- Nima wanted to stay at Ulmeke.

- Hesh believed (and was sure): the shellfish at Kotara do not run out in winter. (Why he wanted to go.)
- Nima believed (and was sure): the walk to Kotara is too long for the old and for small children. (Why she wanted to stay.)

DATA:
Event: dream that changed a mind.
When: year 77, late winter, night.
Place: Sefa (their word; it means "wide water"), a lake, frozen over.
People:
- Dabo: man, 26 years old, of the Kesh band.
- Ama: woman, of the Kesh band; mother of Dabo, dead.
- Pek: man, 29 years old, of the Kesh band.
- Hanu: man, 22 years old, of the Kesh band.
What happened, in order:
- Dabo planned to cross the frozen lake Sefa to hunt on the far shore. Crossing the ice saves a day of walking.
- The night before, Dabo dreamt that his dead mother Ama stood on the ice, and the ice broke under her.
- When he woke, Dabo changed his mind and did not cross the ice.
- He walked around the lake instead, which took him 2 days.
- That same morning, Pek and Hanu crossed the ice and came back safely.
Beliefs (not facts):
- Dabo believed (and was sure): the ice is strong enough to cross. (Before the dream.)
- Dabo believed (but was not sure): the ice will break. (After the dream.)

DATA:
Event: myth retold.
When: year 118, winter, night.
Place: Harum (their word; it means "cold hollow"), the winter camp of the Kesh band.
People:
- Shana: woman, 51 years old, of the Kesh band; teller.

- Shana told the story Tara-mi to 14 listeners at Harum.

- What changed: the sky was added, as the one who put fire in the stone; the name Imra was lost, and she became the first mother; the moss became dry grass.
Their own words for things (use these): "heavy yellow stone".
